28. ACUTE KIDNEY INJURY IN PREGNANCY

1.4% of obstetric admission.

e GFR – Not reliable.

Serum creatinine decreases in pregnancy by 35 µmol/l.

Average = 53 µmol /l.

Abnormal >90 µmol/l => investigate.

40% AKI – unrecognized.

Most common cause = Pre-eclampsia.

Management:

Fluid status Assessment.

Medication review.

Fluid replacement.

Diagnostic work – up.

Involvement of nephrologist if initial management is failed.

Drug dosage Adjustment:

Antibiotics.

Urea – teratogenic >17mmol/l => despite medical treatment need Renal replacement therapy.

Pre – Eclampsia:

Leads to AKI in 1.5 – 2% cases.

Biopsy shows:

Endotheliosis.

Mgso4:

Renal execration.

If Urine output <20ml/hour or creatinine >90 then

Give only 50% dose of Mgso4.

Mgso4 level monitoring 4 – 6 hourly.

Maintain levels 2 – 3.5mol/lit.

Post-partum diuresis (normal).

36 – 48 hours.

Before diuresis, oliguria is normal.

40ml/4 hours (N).

In immediate PP Period.

HELLP:

Cause AKI – 3 – 15%.

Postpartum all parameters deteriorate for 48 hours.

Then recover

Consider TTP.
